entities.summary:
Giacomo Fregoso, also known as Campofregoso, was a pivotal figure in the maritime republic of Genoa during the 14th century.

Born in 1340, Fregoso rose to prominence as a statesman and doge of Genoa, playing a crucial role in shaping the city's politics and economy.

One of his most notable achievements was the establishment of a strong navy that enabled Genoa to challenge the dominance of the Venetian Republic, securing the city's position as a major maritime power.

Fregoso's legacy extends beyond his political career, as he also contributed to the development of the city's artistic and cultural scene, patronizing many notable artists and architects.

Despite his significant impact on Genoa's history, Fregoso's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with many details about his personal life and relationships still shrouded in secrecy.

As a testament to his enduring influence, Fregoso's name continues to be invoked in modern times, with many historians and scholars continuing to study his life and legacy.

In 1974, a plaque was erected in Genoa's historic center, commemorating Fregoso's contributions to the city's development and recognizing his status as one of the most important figures in its history.

Fregoso's story is a fascinating example of how individual leaders can shape the course of history, and his legacy serves as a reminder of the enduring power of human ingenuity and determination.

As the historian Edward Hutton once noted, 'Giacomo Fregoso was a man of great intelligence and activity, who played a leading part in the history of Genoa during the 14th century.'
